messages.content: although i enjoyed the visit, i was tired when i came home. does that sentence sound as if the visit was wrong for me?
no. it says you enjoyed the visit and also felt tired after it. those two things can both be true.
i want to tell my friend that i would like another visit, but maybe a shorter one.
you could say: i enjoyed seeing you. next time, could we have a shorter visit? i think that would help me enjoy the day without being so tired after it.
can i leave out the part about being tired?
yes. you can ask for a shorter visit without giving every reason. for example: i enjoyed seeing you. could we plan a shorter visit next time?
my friend thinks shorter visits mean i want to see her less often.
then you can make the difference clear. you mean less time on each visit, not fewer visits.
write that in a kind way.
i still want to see you often. i just think a shorter time together on each visit would work better for me.
what does although do in my first sentence?
it puts the good visit and the tired feeling together, while making clear that one did not stop the other from being true.
i drew my house with a red door. then i changed the door in the picture to blue. does that mean the real door is blue now?
no. you changed the picture, not the real house. the color in a drawing can be different from the color of the object it is about.
what if the real door was already blue before i drew it?
then your new picture could have the same color as the real door. that still would not mean changing the picture changed the house.
so i should tell you which thing i am asking about?
yes. saying the door in the picture or the door at my house keeps that part clear.
i have not told you the real color. ask me just one question about it.
what color is the door at your house?
it is green. now write one sentence about the picture and one about the house.
the door in the picture is blue. the door at your house is green.
why not make both green?
because you told me the picture is now blue. keeping the real house and the drawing apart keeps the facts you gave clear.
my aunt asked if i would like to come for lunch next week. i want to say yes first, and choose the day later.
you could say: yes, i would love to come for lunch. can we choose the day together later?
i do not want the question to sound as if i am putting off the whole visit.
then keep the yes clear and say which part is still open. for example: i would love to visit. i just need to check which day works before we choose a time.
what if i already know that any day next week is fine for me?
then you can let her choose a day that works for her. you do not need to say you have to check if you already know you are free.
write that message without making up any other reason.
yes, i would love to come for lunch next week. any day works for me, so please choose a day that is good for you.
should i add that i am free every week?
not from what you told me. being free next week does not tell us about every week.
just give me the message again, with no explanation.
yes, i would love to come for lunch next week. any day works for me, so please choose a day that is good for you.
if i say either book is fine, does that mean i want both books?
no. it says you would be happy with one book or the other. to ask for both is to ask for the two books together.
what if i say i like both, but only need one?
then you still only need one. you can choose one even though you like each of them.
i am choosing between a book about a garden and a book about a journey. both sound good.
what would help you choose today: the kind of story you want, how long the book is, or something else?
i want a short story to finish before my visit tomorrow. the garden book is shorter.
then the garden book may work better for that goal, if you can finish it in the time you have. you can still read the journey book another day.
make the answer shorter.
the garden book may work better for your goal today because it is shorter. you can leave the journey book for another day.
write one sentence that has both and one in it.
i like both books, but i will choose one for today.
which word goes before animal: a or an?
an animal is correct.
which word goes before tool?
a tool is correct.
can you give me two full sentences with those words?
an animal is by the tree. a tool is on the table.
if i add small before animal, do i still say an small animal?
no. you would say a small animal. look at the sound of the word that comes right after a or an.
i do not need a long grammar explanation. give me an example with old.
an old tool is on the table.
so the choice is not always about the last word in the group?
right. in an old tool, old comes right after an. in a small animal, small comes right after a.
write one sentence with both objects, but do not add a story.
a small animal is by an old tool.
is that a fact about something outside my window?
no. those are grammar examples. you have not told me that either thing is outside your window.
write a story about a child who wants to build something but first needs to choose a place to work.

a boy wanted to build a small house for his toys. he put his things on the kitchen table, but his mother was getting lunch ready there. he asked if he could use the floor by the window. she said there was room, as long as he kept the door clear. he carried his things to the new place and began with one wall. after lunch, his sister came to look. she asked where the toys would sleep, and he showed her the small room he had made. together, they added a door and a roof. when they finished, he put the toys inside and moved his tools out of the way.
did he build the house on the kitchen table?
no. that was his first idea for a place to work, but he built it on the floor by the window.
what did his mother ask him to keep clear?
the door.
why did his sister ask about a place to sleep?
she was asking about part of the toy house. the story does not give any other reason for her question.
make the story end with him leaving the work for tomorrow instead.
when lunch was ready, he left the small house by the window. he put his tools away and chose to add the door and roof tomorrow.
in a story i am writing, i can walk through the wall of my old house. can i tell it using i went through the wall?
you can use that sentence in a story about something impossible. it helps to make clear that it is a story, so it does not sound like something you did in the real world.
i want an example story, not to say i really did it.
then you can begin: in my story, i went through the wall of my old house.
what if i want it to be about a person opening a door instead, so it could happen in real life?
you could say: i opened the door of my old house and went inside.
does could happen mean it did happen?
no. something being possible does not tell us that it happened. it just says that part of the story could happen.
say that another way.
no. a person can open a door and go inside, but that does not tell us anyone did it in the real world.
write only the sentence about the door.
i opened the door of my old house and went inside.
i remember that my cousin is visiting tomorrow, but i forgot whether she is bringing lunch or just coming after lunch.
that detail changes what you need to have ready. you could ask her before making food for both of you.
can you tell me which one she said?
i do not have that information from your message. you gave me two possible plans, but not which one she chose.
write a short question that does not make it sound as if i forgot the whole visit.
i am happy you are coming tomorrow. are we having lunch together, or are you coming after lunch?
make that message a little shorter.
are we having lunch together tomorrow, or are you coming after lunch?
she said she is coming after lunch. should i make a meal for her?
she is coming after lunch, so you can plan for the visit without making lunch part of it. you can ask if she wants anything when she comes.
give me only what i now know about the plan.
she is coming after lunch. you can plan for the visit, but you have not said you will eat lunch together.
what part did i remember right from the start?
you remembered that she is visiting tomorrow.
in this story, my brother and sister own a book together. my sister says it is mine. is that clear about whose book it is?
it says she thinks of it as hers, but it leaves out your brother. if they own it together, she could say it is our book.
use our in a short answer.
she could say: it is our book. that makes clear that she is talking about herself and your brother together.
what if she says i am reading it now, so it is only mine?
reading it now does not change who has it to keep. she can have the reading turn while the book is still for both of them.
my brother says she can keep it from now on. what changes?
then the story has new information about who will keep the book. if he gives his part to her, calling it her book can now be right.
say that more simply.
your brother said she could keep it from now on. that changes the story about whose book it is.
what stayed the same while she was only reading it before he said that?
her reading turn did not by itself change the book from theirs together to hers alone.
i finally learned the first part of a song. i do not know all of it yet, but i am happy.
that sounds like a good start. learning one part gives you something real to build on.
my sister says i should wait until i know the whole song before feeling happy about it.
you can be happy about one part without saying the whole task is finished. those are different things.
i want a quiet reply, not a long explanation about working hard.
i am happy that part feels good to you. you can enjoy it as it is.
give me a shorter kind answer.
you can enjoy the part you know now.
what if i forget some of it tomorrow?
you still spent time learning today. if you forget a part tomorrow, you could go back to the part you remember and try it again slowly.
keep that last explanation shorter.
you still learned something today. if you forget a part tomorrow, you can try it again.
end with one kind sentence and no question.
you can enjoy the part you learned today.
i need bread and milk for breakfast. fruit would be nice, but breakfast can work without it. what should go first on my list for the market?
bread and milk should go first because you said you need them. fruit can come after because it is something you would like but can do without.
give me a shorter answer about the order.
put bread and milk first on the list. put fruit after them because breakfast can work without it.
i only have enough money for two of those three things.
then choose bread and milk. you said you need those, while breakfast can work without fruit.
say just what i should choose and why.
choose bread and milk. you said breakfast needs those two things and can work without fruit.
what if i now say i have milk at home already?
then you do not need to buy it again for this breakfast, unless you need more than you already have. you can check how much there is before choosing what to buy.
give me a simple question to ask myself.
do i have enough milk at home for breakfast?
what should change on the list if the answer is yes?
you can leave milk off the list for this breakfast.
is my book there?
which book do you mean, and which place are you asking about?
i mean the red book on my desk. i cannot see it from here.
i do not have a way to see your desk from those words. if you last saw it there, that gives a place to check, but i do not know if it is there now.
explain that in a more simple way.
i cannot see your desk. i can help you think about where to look, but i do not know whether the red book is there now.
why not just say yes to make me feel better?
because yes would sound as if i knew it was there. a kind answer should still keep clear what i know and what i do not know.
i found it on the desk. now can you say it is there?
yes, from what you just told me, you found the red book on the desk.
write one short sentence with that information.
the red book is on your desk, from what you said.
what changed between the first question and the last answer?
you gave me new information after looking for the book.
write a short story about a girl who sees a cloud and thinks a walk might have to change.

a girl was getting ready to walk with her friend. when she looked out, she saw a large cloud. she thought there might be rain before they got home. instead of saying the walk was impossible, she called her friend and asked what they should do. they chose to check the weather again before leaving. while they waited, they sat by the window and talked. after a while, they looked outside together and made a plan using what they could see then. the story does not say whether they finally walked or stayed home.
why did you leave the end open?
the girl was thinking about a possible change. we can follow that part of the story without knowing which choice she finally made.
use only our simple words for that explanation.
the girl had not yet chosen whether to walk. the story keeps that choice open while she gets more information.
did seeing a cloud make rain a fact she knew for sure?
no. seeing a cloud gave her a reason to think about rain, but it did not tell her for sure what would happen.
ask me a question about what she knew.
what did the girl see before calling her friend?
she saw a large cloud. give me just that answer again.
a large cloud.
i am reading a story about two friends on a journey. can we talk about it without you telling me the end?
yes. tell me which part you have read and what you want to talk about. i can keep the conversation to the details you give.
i have read that one friend wants to return home and the other wants to keep going.
that gives them different things they want from the journey. what do you think each friend wants from the trip?
i do not want to make up a reason that may not be in the part i have read.
then we can stay with what is already on the page. you know one wants home and the other wants to go on. what did they say to each other about that?
they have not talked to each other about it yet.
then you know what each wants, but not how a conversation between them will go. we can talk about that difference without making up the next part.
ask one question that i can answer from what i already told you.
which friend wants to return home?
the first one. now write a short sentence about what each friend wants.
one friend wants to return home, while the other wants to keep going.
does that tell me the end of the story?
no. it only gives the information you already told me.
i took my book inside because rain was starting. which part is the reason?
rain was starting is the reason you gave for taking the book inside.
can i change it to rain was starting because i took my book inside?
that would change which thing was the reason. it would sound as if taking the book inside made the rain start. that is not what your first sentence said.
give me a more simple explanation.
that would change which thing was the reason. your first sentence says the rain made you take the book inside, not that moving the book made the rain start.
write it with the reason first.
because rain was starting, i took my book inside.
does moving the because part change what happened?
not in that sentence. both give the rain as the reason you took the book inside.
answer another way.
no. both sentences say you took the book inside because of the rain.
what if i leave because out and say i took my book inside. rain was starting.
then you give two facts, but you do not make the reason as clear as you do with because.
my friend asked whether i am ready for her visit. the room is clean, but i have not made lunch. can i say everything is ready?
not if lunch is part of what you mean by everything. you can say the room is ready and that lunch is still to be made.
she told me she was bringing food. i forgot that when i asked you.
then lunch may not be a task you need to finish yourself. you could check whether she needs anything for the food, but you do not have to make a whole meal just because it is not made at your house.
write a short reply that says what i have done.
the room is ready. thank you for bringing lunch. is there anything you would like me to have for the meal?
i do not want a question in this reply.
the room is ready. thank you for bringing lunch. i am happy you are coming.
give me a shorter message with the same meaning.
the room is ready, and i am happy you are bringing lunch.
why was the answer different after i remembered her message?
because bringing the food was already her part of the plan. that changed whether you needed to make lunch.
last week i wanted a large desk. now i think a small one would work better in my room. my brother says one of those answers must be a lie.
your choice can change when you think about new information. a large desk can have been your wish last week, while a small one can be your choice now. that does not have to make either answer false.
i checked the space yesterday and found that the large desk would leave no room for my chair.
then you have a reason for the new choice. the smaller desk may give you room for both the desk and chair.
explain my choice using what i found when i checked the space.
you checked the space and found the large desk would leave no room for your chair. that gave you a reason to choose a smaller desk.
does changing my mind mean i never liked the large desk?
no. you could still like it while choosing something that works better in the room.
write one sentence to explain my choice without saying anything about my brother.
i liked the large desk, but the smaller one leaves room for my chair, so it works better here.
give me only the sentence.
i liked the large desk, but the smaller one leaves room for my chair, so it works better here.
write a story about someone who asks which way to go before leaving a house.

a boy wanted to walk from the house of his aunt to the library. she said to go left. he asked which way to face when choosing left. they went to the front door together, and she showed him the road. he checked the next turn on his map and asked another question. when he understood, he said thank you and left.
tell the story again with fewer details.

a boy wanted to walk to the library. his aunt told him to go left, but he asked which way to look first. she showed him from the front door, and they checked the next turn on his map. then he said thank you and left.
why was left alone not enough?
he did not know which way he should be looking when he chose left.
did asking make him wrong?
no. asking helped him understand before leaving.
what did the map help him check?
the next turn.
make this shorter: i do not want to leave the book at school because i need it at home this evening.
i need the book at home this evening, so i do not want to leave it at school.
can i make it even shorter by saying i want to leave it at school?
no. leaving out not changes the meaning. it would say the opposite of what you first wanted.
give me a more simple explanation.
no. leaving out not changes the meaning. the shorter sentence would say you want to leave the book at school, but your first sentence said you do not.
give me a short sentence that keeps the meaning.
i want to take the book home for this evening.
does that still say why i do not want to leave it at school?
it keeps the idea that you want the book at home, but it does not make the need as clear. you could say: i need the book at home this evening.
give me only that last sentence.
i need the book at home this evening.
what is the most important thing to check when making a sentence shorter?
keep the important meaning. a word like not is important when leaving it out would change the answer.
i want to tell my grandfather about my week. should i call or write a letter?
what would work best for him and for you? a call can give you time to ask and answer questions together. a letter gives him something he can read again later.
give me the difference in a more simple way.
a call gives you time to ask and answer questions together. a letter gives him something he can read again later.
he likes keeping a letter, but he also likes hearing my voice.
you do not have to choose the same thing every time. you could write a letter about this week and have a short call another day, if that works for both of you.
i only want a plan for today.
for today, you could write a letter if he most wants something to keep and read again. if he wants to talk with you now, a call may work better.
give me a question i could ask him.
would you like a call today, or would you rather have a letter about my week?
what if i want to make the choice without asking him today?
then use what you already know about him to choose. you can still ask another day what he enjoys most.
